statement: Compute session-RPE load as duration x CR-10 rating for every run and use it as the primary, device-independent internal-load metric. Ask for one rating after each run with constant wording and visible CR-10 anchors.
appliesTo: All users and run types, including those with no HR data

statement: Prompt for the RPE rating about 30 minutes after the session as the default. The abstracts do not state timing, so this is a design default, and the rating must stay editable.

Store sRPE load and HR-based load (TRIMP) as separate fields. Do not add them or apply a fixed conversion, because absolute sRPE values are systematically higher than HR-based scores. Interpret each against the user's own history.

Accept wrist optical HR as an input to HR-based load for steady running (treadmill or flat road), where pooled mean bias against a criterion is about -0.5 bpm and most devices have rc 0.88 to 0.93, but still apply per-sample sanity filters and record device make/model.
appliesTo: Wrist-HR runs on treadmill or steady, flat terrain

statement: For hilly, trail, interval or non-running activities, or when an HR-quality check fails, do not compute HR-based load from wrist HR. Use chest-strap HR if present, otherwise sRPE. Specific check thresholds (jumps, gaps, cadence-like HR) are a design choice with no evidenced value; start conservatively and tune on real data.
value: low (reject for TRIMP; fall back to sRPE)
appliesTo: Wrist-HR hills, trails, intervals, strength and cycling; all runs failing the quality check

statement: Implement Banister TRIMP as duration x HR-reserve fraction x weighting, with exponent b = 1.92 for men and 1.67 for women (leading weights commonly cited as 0.64 and 0.86). These constants and the original formula are not verified in this corpus: Banister 1991 is not indexed and no checked abstract states them. Ship as a labelled default, show the formula, and use the male constant (or an explicit user setting) when sex is unspecified.
appliesTo: Runs with trustworthy HR plus resting and max HR

statement: Where the user supplies a lactate-threshold or field-test HR profile, offer an individualized exponential-weighted TRIMP as an opt-in upgrade over the generic weighting. Use TRIMP trend over weeks, not single sessions, in build/recovery logic, and keep thresholds from this evidence out of hard rules (n = 8).

Treat sRPE, Banister TRIMP and running TSS as interchangeable load inputs for plan logic; no method is shown to be superior (model-vs-performance r 0.60 to 0.70 in seven runners). Compute whichever are available and make plan decisions against the athlete's own history, not absolute cross-method values.
value: no single winner; sRPE primary for availability

statement: When both sRPE and HR load exist, compute each as a z-score against the user's own rolling history and show the session as divergent when the gap exceeds a threshold. Do not auto-correct either value. The default 1.5 SD with at least 8 prior sessions is an untested design choice.
value: 1.5 SD (design default; at least 8 prior sessions)
appliesTo: Sessions with both sRPE and trusted HR load

statement: Keep external load (distance, duration, pace, elevation, running power) and internal load (TRIMP, sRPE) as separate stored series. Use internal load for adaptation/readiness features and external load for volume and mechanical-load features. Never label an external metric as physiological stress, and present load as single-athlete decision support, not an injury predictor.
Do not use device-reported energy expenditure (kcal) as an input to load, fuelling or plan calculations.

Use device-reported lap and total distance rather than rebuilding it from raw points. Do not derive instantaneous or gradient-adjusted pace from raw 1 Hz wrist-GNSS speed; smooth it. Treat watch elevation gain as noisy (vertical IQR 13.35 m for one 2014 wrist watch) and prefer barometric or map-corrected elevation. Down-weight pace-based intensity on slow uphill segments and use HR or RPE there. Evidence is indirect (skiing, one old watch).
value: smoothed speed; device total distance; elevation flagged noisy

statement: Ingest running power only as an external-load metric tagged with the source device. Accept Stryd power for load and intensity features; flag Garmin, Polar and RunScribe power as low confidence; never mix devices within a power zone or load series.

Do not use watch-reported lactate-threshold pace as a training-zone anchor without confirmation from a time trial or race (it overestimated lab LT pace by 12.7 to 25.8% MAPE). Treat watch LT HR (MAE 8.9 to 11.4 bpm, r 0.13 to 0.67) only as a rough starting value with user override; prefer zones from observed max HR and recent hard efforts.
value: LT pace untrusted until confirmed; LT HR advisory only

statement: Do not apply a skin-tone-specific HR correction. Model wrist-HR quality per device and activity, flag low quality, fall back to sRPE, and offer a chest-strap recommendation to every user who wants accurate HR load.
